questions.q: In a triangle, $\angle A=40^\circ$, $a=10$, and $\angle B=65^\circ$. Find $b$, rounded to the nearest hundredth.
questions.answer: By the Law of Sines, $\dfrac{b}{\sin B}=\dfrac{a}{\sin A} \Rightarrow b=\dfrac{10\sin65^\circ}{\sin40^\circ}\approx14.10$.

questions.q: In a triangle, $\angle A=30^\circ$, $\angle B=75^\circ$, and $a=6$. Find $\angle C$ first, then explain how you would find side $c$.
questions.answer: $\angle C=180^\circ-30^\circ-75^\circ=75^\circ$. Then use $\dfrac{c}{\sin C}=\dfrac{a}{\sin A}$ to solve for $c$.

questions.q: A triangle has $a=10$, $b=6$, and included angle $C=40^\circ$. Find $c$, rounded to the nearest hundredth.
Explain when you should use the Law of Cosines instead of the Law of Sines to solve a triangle.
questions.answer: The Law of Cosines is used when you know two sides and the included angle (SAS), or all three sides (SSS) — cases where the Law of Sines can't be set up directly because no side-angle pair is fully known.

If $\cos x=-\dfrac{1}{2}$ and $x$ is in Quadrant II (so $\sin x=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$), find $\cos2x$.
Convert the polar point $\left(8,\,150^\circ\right)$ to rectangular coordinates.

Convert the rectangular point $\left(-3,\,3\sqrt{3}\right)$ to polar coordinates $(r,\theta)$ with $r>0$ and $0^\circ\leq\theta<360^\circ$.
questions.working: Since the point is in Quadrant II, $\theta=120^\circ$ (from $\tan\theta=\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{-3}=-\sqrt{3}$, adjusted for the correct quadrant).

In a triangle, $\angle A=135^\circ$, $a=16$, and $\angle B=45^\circ$. Find $b$.
questions.answer: By the Law of Sines, $\dfrac{b}{\sin B}=\dfrac{a}{\sin A}$, so $b=a\cdot\dfrac{\sin45^\circ}{\sin135^\circ}=16(1)=16$.

questions.q: In a triangle, $\angle A=90^\circ$, $a=8$, and $\angle B=30^\circ$. Find $b$.
questions.answer: By the Law of Sines, $\dfrac{b}{\sin B}=\dfrac{a}{\sin A}$, so $b=a\cdot\dfrac{\sin30^\circ}{\sin90^\circ}=8(1/2)=4$.

questions.q: In a triangle, $\angle A=135^\circ$, $a=3$, and $\angle B=45^\circ$. Find $b$.
questions.answer: By the Law of Sines, $\dfrac{b}{\sin B}=\dfrac{a}{\sin A}$, so $b=a\cdot\dfrac{\sin45^\circ}{\sin135^\circ}=3(1)=3$.

questions.q: In a triangle, $\angle A=135^\circ$, $a=17$, and $\angle B=45^\circ$. Find $b$.
questions.answer: By the Law of Sines, $\dfrac{b}{\sin B}=\dfrac{a}{\sin A}$, so $b=a\cdot\dfrac{\sin45^\circ}{\sin135^\circ}=17(1)=17$.

questions.q: In a triangle, $\angle A=30^\circ$, $a=12$, and $\angle B=90^\circ$. Find $b$.
questions.answer: By the Law of Sines, $\dfrac{b}{\sin B}=\dfrac{a}{\sin A}$, so $b=a\cdot\dfrac{\sin90^\circ}{\sin30^\circ}=12(2)=24$.
